transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, what brings me in is... I'm having a lot of trouble staying focused at work. I'm a construction manager, and I'll start a safety briefing or sit down for a plan review, trying really hard to pay attention. But within just a couple of minutes, my mind is already off on three other job problems. Because of that, I end up missing things—details I know I should have caught. It's really starting to become a serious issue for me.
Has this trouble focusing been a pattern you've noticed since childhood or adolescence, or is it something that started more recently, say in the past few months?

No, it's... it's definitely not recent. It's been going on since I was a kid. 

I remember back in elementary school, my teachers were already telling my parents about it. They'd complain that I couldn't stay in my seat, or that I talked out of turn a lot. I was always losing my homework, too, and just... rushing through directions before I really understood what I was actually supposed to do. So, yeah, it's been a pattern pretty much my whole life.
Aside from the trouble focusing, do you find yourself worrying excessively about multiple things—work, health, family—more days than not, and having trouble controlling that worry?

Not really, no. I mean... I get stressed when I mess up at work because I missed a detail, but I wouldn't say I'm a worrier. I don't really sit around stressing about my health or my family or anything like that. It's not a constant worry about everything, it's mostly just... frustration that I can't seem to keep my head straight on the job site.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless, or noticing a loss of interest or pleasure in things you'd usually enjoy?

No, I haven't been feeling like that. I'm not depressed or anything. I still like doing the things I usually do, like fishing on the weekends. It's just the work stuff that's really getting to me right now.
These days, do you notice yourself feeling restless, fidgeting, or having trouble sitting still, or find yourself interrupting others or acting impulsively?

Yeah, definitely. Sitting still is really tough for me. Like, if we have meetings where everybody else can just sit through the whole thing, I just can't do it. I’m always the guy standing up, walking over to get coffee, or stepping outside to check on something. I basically just end up making some excuse to move around because staying in the chair the whole time just doesn't work for me.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out GAD (no excessive worry) and MDD (no depressed mood/anhedonia). Confirmed childhood-onset inattentive symptoms plus current hyperactive-impulsive symptoms (restlessness, difficulty sitting still), supporting combined presentation consistent with F90.0.
